verdict.tagline: Endless number growth stalls against technical friction and abandoned updates.
for_you_if: you enjoy idle games centered on watching numbers grow
you like automating tasks with managers and angel investors
not_for_you_if: you encounter startup errors and hardware overheating
you want active events and continued developer support
you dislike microtransactions pushing pay-to-win elements

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game encounters startup and launch failures, specifically presenting resolution errors or freezing on the title screen after selecting graphics settings.

citations.review_text: It was a decent mobile game, but it doesn't even run on PC.  Always fails to achieve whatever resolution I choose in the launcher, which IMHO is one the most basic simple things that an app can do.  But for some reason these devs couldn't get their game to do even that.  I understand Hyper Hippo's desire to extract even more cash from this IP with as little effort as humanly possible, but why didn't they at least try to make it functional?

Unfortunately, i can't rate nor recommend the game if i can't even play it. This automatically makes it a hard pass in my eyes.

All resolution switches have failed

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the game lacks in-game options to cap frame rates or adjust volume levels.

citations.review_text: So, first, this apparently always online game greeted me with a "Connection Error". Then, after restarting, it sat on the title card forever. I switched to Proton 9, as this game wants to default to not using proton, and it suddenly started working. However, it then runs at 1500fps, and has absolutely no options menu to cap it with. Like, I get it's just a free visual revamp of a free game, but come on.
why tf does this game run worse than minecraft its so unoptomized and loud af with no volume slider

claims.claim: Reviewers note that events are absent from the Steam version of the game and are only available on mobile.

citations.review_text: It is a perfect 1:1 port of the mobile version, however it's filled with microtransactions and no longer gets updates. The only reason I still play the Steam version is because my save data is on it and as far as I know, there's no way to back it up. It's still a good game though.

Its a pretty fun game, although the most fun part of the game was always to play events and try to get a high spot on the leaderboard for items etc, now theres no events anymore on steam and the only way to play them is on mobile

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Experienced players engage with idle mechanics, offline progression, and resetting for angel investors, while grappling with microtransactions and basic gameplay loops.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features offline progression, allowing earnings to accumulate while the player is away.

citations.review_text: I absolutely love this game. It's good on old devices, it doesn't require much, and it grows offline.

Hiring managers is easily one of the most satisfying parts of the game. Once they take over the repetitive work, I can focus more on unlocking upgrades, and expanding into new businesses. Combined with offline earnings and angel investors, the automation keeps the progression moving even when I’m not actively playing. It’s a simple but addictive idle game that always gives me another milestone to chase.

Usually in incremental games I prefer when there is an option to put the numbers in scientific notation so that they can make sense. This game is the exact opposite, no option and for good reason.

Try and wrap your head around the absurdity of an undecillionaire as numbers lose all meaning only for an achievement for being a Googolaire to pop.

The game is a fantastic satire of capitalism, even down to the unnecessary micro transactions that try to squeeze every penny out of you; luckily DLC is not necessary to have your monkey brain hijacked by seeing numbers go up and squeeze out the last remaining dopamine in my brain before going back to the horror show that is the real world.

As a side note: this is the kind of game that only requires you to interact with it for a few minutes each day as progress happens offline.

Um jogo longo, "roda offline" muito bom para quando você quer jogar algo e colocar zero esforço, ao mesmo tempo, é um jogo que demora bastante para zerar sem gastar dinheiro e oferece eventos semanais.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that hiring managers automates repetitive tasks and lets players focus on upgrades and expanding businesses.

citations.review_text: Hiring managers is easily one of the most satisfying parts of the game. Once they take over the repetitive work, I can focus more on unlocking upgrades, and expanding into new businesses. Combined with offline earnings and angel investors, the automation keeps the progression moving even when I’m not actively playing. It’s a simple but addictive idle game that always gives me another milestone to chase.

Pay to Win and watch your hours waste away.

AdVenture Capitalist is an incremental game.  These games are all about attempting to boost some main statistic, in this case money, as high as you can over time.  The true gameplay is simply waiting for time to pass so you accumulate enough money to be able to purchase the next upgrade so that your number goes up more quickly.

While the basis of incremental style games are all the same, some are more complex than others, and Adventure Capitalist is as simple as they come.  You have 10 "stores" that you can run.  You begin by purchasing a lemonade stand and you click the stand every time you earn money to get the stand to make money again.  Each time you earn money, you can reinvest it into your business by purchasing more of them, or after some time, hiring manages to hit the button for you.  Each time you buy enough of a store, you'll multiply that store's profits.  On top of this, you can purchase upgrades that multiply store profits again.

After you've earned enough money, you can rest your progress and earn "Angel Investors" usually just called angels in the game.  Each angel boosts your overall earning by 2 percent, so the more angels you have, the faster your number grows, and the faster you earn additional angels.  

This is the core loop of the game.  You earn as much as you can as quickly as possible, and then you wait to earn more angels, reset your progress, and do it all over again.

There is no story and there are no unfolding mechanics, it's JUST clicking a button and earning more money.

It's VERY easy to get sucked into this game because of how simple it is, and it you don't mind spending a lot of time pressing a button to see a number go up, then you can enjoy this game a lot.  However, I think that people can do much better, and I think people should avoid wasting time and effort on a game like this.

[h1]Do not play this time waster.[/h1]
AdVenture Capitalist is the worst of its kind in the idle genre.

The gameplay loop is mindless and boring. Progression is slow no matter if you have an active or passive playstyle. It counts on your brain not wanting anything more than the dopamine hit of "number go up". It's addictive in only the worst ways. There are far better idle games that at least pretend to respect your time. This game [b]hates you.[/b]

Live events are a joke. Some have unique gimmicks, but are ultimately just another lazy way for the devs to keep your game open. Leaderboards are rife with cheating and offer rewards that are disproportionately low compared to the effort required.

This game pushes microtransactions [b]HARD.[/b] It's [i]suffocating.[/i] Meaningful progression is practically impossible without spending money and the devs know it. For dedicated players, avoiding in-game purchases effectively becomes a core game mechanic. Despite the satirical-looking name, the execution isn't a parody of capitalism; it is a very literal, predatory implementation of it with a cartoon artstyle.

My brain loves incremental games. This one actively harmed mine.

If you STILL want to play it, this is what I think is the optimal way:

Events: (boring part)

You'll have to play every event and place preferably among the top 5 each time, netting you some timeskips and megabucks among other things. This might not seem that bad but this is why it sucks (long explenation incoming, feel free to skip): 
There is a multiplier in these events you can turn on that shuts off after not clicking it for 10 seconds. This means you constantly need to have your mouse on the multiplier with an autoclicker, and sometimes buying buildings, upgrades and managers before quickly getting your mouse back without loosing this boost. The boost is well over 10x in most events so it is essential you don't lose it. If you lose it there is a 4 hour cooldown, but you can have your autoclicker over and shorten this by 1 second every click, in my case it took about 12 minutes. 
Anyway, main focus during these events is to get to a certain point in the late game where you can do the  building challenges within 5-10 minutes or shorter. The cash and angel challenges are usually way longer and will come automatically so no need to hard focus these. 
Doing this all day for the first two days, 3 hours a day for the next two days and ignoring last day I scored 3rd place, with 2nd place being very doable with some added effort. 

The main thing you want in these events are megabucks and opther rewards such as time skips and free angel claims from scoring high on the leaderboard, and gold from getting a certain amount of points in the event.

cohorts.label: 100h+
cohorts.summary: Long-term players highlight discontinued support, connection problems, and hardware overheating on newer processors.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the Steam version of the game no longer receives updates or support.

citations.review_text: There are just infinitely better idle/incremental games out there that have a lot more soul than this one. Game is abandoned and no longer supported/updated. AdCap is decently fun until you reach the last 10-25% of Earth, as it becomes INSANELY unbalanced and monotonous. Events are cool until they're not, which happens pretty quick, as they are often re-skins of the same event you had just played last time. The game isn't discreet about microtransations either, which are pretty hilarious for a game so old and essentially left to rot. The only good things about this game are nostalgia and the mars planet.

(THE STEAM VERSION OF THIS GAME NO LONGER RECIVES UPDATES) (I 100% completed this game )

When you first start playing this game it's fun as you progress quickly but as you slowly reach endgame it gets to a point where the only way to progress quickly is to buy stuff from the gold and Mega ticket shop. However the only way to earn gold for free is milestones and events. Milestones happen rarely as the progression is slow so the main way to get gold and tickets are events. The events function similarly to the main game but gives you 4 quests that gives you point and earning a x amount of points will give you rewards and has a leaderboard system. but what ends up happening is you don't have enough time to get all the rewards unless you are actively playing the game (the booster system via clicking to keep the booster active)  and the leaderboard it sweaty af. So the main way to progress is ether wait or play the events actively or spend money on a game that no longer receives updates.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game is not optimized for new M-series processors and runs only on an older Intel version, causing hardware to get very hot.

citations.review_text: Not bad for a start BUT then I noticed that my Mac was getting very hot - it turned out that it an only version for Intel and it was not optimized for the new M-series processors

While the game does everything as advertised, its a massive waste of time and electricity. I have spent 280 hours in game os of now and man do i regret it. The game right up my alley but the post playing regret is high for me. it has nothing exciting, just waiting. it keeps me anxious when i play it, and even if i kept it on in the background, i was never able to focus on what im actually doing. I may continue playing it though because i am a completionist and want to finish the game and getting all its achievemnets. If you still wish to play it, I wish you good luck and hope you dont regret the time you spent on it.
